hints.title: Disjoint Ancestry Branch Obstacle
hints.text: In an arbitrary binary tree without ordering properties, nodes p and q can appear anywhere. If the current root matches p or q, or if p and q lie in opposite branches, what does that imply about the ancestor?

hints.title: Branch Separation Invariant
hints.text: If p and q are found in separate left and right subtrees of a node, that node is their lowest common ancestor. If both reside in one subtree, the ancestor lies entirely within that subtree.

hints.title: Post-Order LCA Resolution Procedure
hints.text: If root is null or equals p or q, return root. Recursively search left and right subtrees. If both return non-null, root is the lowest common ancestor. Otherwise, return whichever subtree returned non-null.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Single post-order traversal visiting each node at most once with call stack bounded by tree height.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Storing parent pointers or root paths for both nodes requires extra O(N) memory and multiple passes.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(H) recursion stack space with no additional data structures.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Base case returning root when root matches p or q directly.
